server.name: streamloop-mcp
server.title: Streamloop MCP
server.description: Run video on a loop 24/7 to YouTube, Twitch, Facebook or any RTMP destination: create and schedule streams, upload or import media, arrange playlists, connect destinations, build live scenes and check credits and live status.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Streamloop loops video 24/7 to YouTube or any RTMP destination for the signed-in account.
SET UP A LOOP, in order: create_stream; media in (create_upload → PUT → complete_upload for a
local file; discover_external_media → import_upload_from_url for any https url, attachments
included); list_playlists(streamId) → apply_playlist_operations on its video playlist; a
destination (list_destinations, else get_connection_hints(platform)) → add_stream_destination;
check_stream_readiness → start_stream or schedule_stream. Nothing needs publishing first.
LIVE STREAM: after editing its playlist, swap_live_playlist puts the edit on air.
SCENES: edit the draft with scene_get/scene_set; publish_scene; set_stream_scene (stopped
stream); start_stream.
RULES: schedule times need an explicit UTC offset (the user's clock is not UTC); weekly
repeats use the UTC weekday. An empty list is often the wrong workspace: check
get_selected_workspace. Ids are prefixed (stream_, pl_, obj_, dest_, scn_...): read them from
a list tool, never invent one. Errors carry a code: branch on it. A stream that will not start
with no config issue: get_billing_overview (credits; buying them is dashboard-only).
Full guide: resource streamloop://guide.

tool.name: start_stream
tool.title: Start stream
tool.description: Start streaming now, looping the stream's playlist (or playing its scene) until it is stopped. THIS PUTS VIDEO IN FRONT OF THE PUBLIC, so confirm with the user first unless they just asked for it. Requires a destination plus either a playable video playlist (at least one item) or an attached published scene (set_stream_scene) — check_stream_readiness reports what is missing without changing anything, and is worth calling first. A failed pre-flight is NOT an error: the call succeeds and the answer's `state` is `invalid` — read `state` first: invalid means refused, with `issues` saying why (fix them and start again); `preparing` means accepted. Media facts (duration, sound) arrive about 15-25 s after an upload completes, so a playlist of just-finished uploads can be refused until then. Other refusals (a state that cannot start, a guard failing at the moment of starting) are errors. Credits are NOT part of the pre-flight: the balance is verified when the stream actually activates, so an otherwise-ready stream can still fail to start on an empty wallet — get_billing_overview is what tells you that. A playlist loop takes the playlist as it currently is, with nothing to publish first; a scene plays its published version (publish_scene). Asynchronous: the stream reports a starting state immediately and is live within about a minute. To start at a future time (or every day) use schedule_stream instead. Returns state, started (false when refused), issues (when refused) and startStream (the stream: id, name, state).

state.description: The stream's state after the call: preparing = accepted (live within about a minute); invalid = refused by the pre-flight, see issues.

issues.description: When refused: what blocks the start, as check_stream_readiness says it.

started.description: false when the pre-flight refused it (state invalid).

startStream.description: The stream after the call: id, name, state.

tool.name: create_stream
tool.title: Create stream
tool.description: Use this to set up a new loop or a stream for a scene. The stream is created empty and CANNOT start until it has (1) a destination — add_stream_destination with one from list_destinations, or get_connection_hints for how to make one — plus (2) either a playable video playlist (at least one item) or an attached published scene (set_stream_scene). Creating a stream also creates its two empty playlists (one video, one audio): for a loop, find them with list_playlists(streamId) and fill them with apply_playlist_operations — a playlist loop needs nothing published before the first start. Media facts (duration, sound) of an upload arrive about 15-25 s after it completes: a start right after uploading can be refused (state invalid) until then. When it runs is schedule_stream's job. Returns the new stream under createStream: id (stream_...), name, state, quality, framerate, createdAt.

tool.name: update_stream
tool.title: Update stream
tool.description: Change a stream's settings (name, quality, framerate, duration, storage, backup ingest) and/or its YouTube broadcast settings via the `youtube` object. Where it publishes is add_stream_destination / set_stream_destination_enabled / remove_stream_destination; when it runs is schedule_stream. The `youtube` settings only apply when one of the stream's destinations is a YouTube channel connected through Streamloop — not a custom RTMP destination, and not YouTube reached through a raw RTMP URL and key — and are otherwise skipped with a notice. Set retryMirror=true to re-attempt mirroring the schedule onto YouTube after a reconnect or a quota recovery. PARTIAL SUCCESS: settings are applied first, so if the YouTube settings then fail, `stream` still reflects the applied settings and `youtubeSettingsError` explains the YouTube failure — the settings change is NOT rolled back.

tool.name: schedule_stream
tool.title: Schedule stream
tool.description: Set the window a stream runs in, once or on a repeat, and arm it. The stream must already be startable — a destination plus either a playable video playlist or an attached published scene (check_stream_readiness) — otherwise the window arrives and the start fails. repeat=daily re-arms the window exactly 24h later; repeat=weekly re-arms +7 days, or on the weekdays given in `days`. Both repeats REQUIRE scheduleEndAt and a window shorter than 24h; a one-off (repeat=none, the default) may be open-ended. `days` are UTC weekdays of the start instant, so a 9pm Monday Eastern window repeats on TUESDAY — the result echoes the committed window in UTC with its UTC weekday so this is visible. Replaces any existing window; cancel_stream_schedule disarms it. Returns the stream (id, name, state, scheduleStartAt, scheduleEndAt, scheduleRepeat, scheduleRepeatDays) and committedWindow: the window in UTC, its UTC start weekday, and the times exactly as you sent them.

days.description: Only with repeat=weekly: the UTC weekdays the window starts on (distinct). Omit for the same UTC weekday as scheduleStartAt, every 7 days.

repeat.description: How the window recurs: once when omitted, every 24h, or every 7 days (or on `days`). A repeat needs scheduleEndAt.

scheduleEndAt.description: When the stream should stop. Needed for a daily or weekly repeat, less than 24h after the start; omit for a one-off that runs until stopped. An instant in the user's own time zone, with that zone's offset: 6am US Eastern daylight time is 2026-09-22T06:00:00-04:00. The user's clock numbers are not UTC.

scheduleStartAt.description: When the stream should start. An instant in the user's own time zone, with that zone's offset: 6am US Eastern daylight time is 2026-09-22T06:00:00-04:00. The user's clock numbers are not UTC.

endAtUTC.description: End instant in UTC; null for an open-ended one-off.

asRequested.description: startAt, endAt and offset exactly as sent.

startWeekdayUTC.description: UTC weekday of the start: the day a weekly repeat runs on.

committedWindow.description: The committed window restated in UTC, to check the time zone was read as meant.

tool.name: check_stream_readiness
tool.title: Check stream readiness
tool.description: Answer 'would start_stream work right now?' without changing anything. Runs the same pre-flight configuration checks a start does and returns ready plus every blocking issue — typically a missing or archived destination, an empty video playlist, media too big for the stream's storage, or, for a stream playing a scene, a scene that is missing, not published or invalid. It does NOT check whether uploads have finished processing: a playlist takes only completed uploads, but their media facts (duration, sound) arrive about 15-25 s after an upload completes, so wait that long after uploading before starting. Credits and YouTube live eligibility are deliberately NOT part of it (both are re-checked at the moment the stream activates), so ready=true means correctly configured, not guaranteed to go live — pair it with get_billing_overview when a ready stream still will not start. Call it before start_stream and before relying on a schedule_stream window. Returns streamReadiness: ready, and issues[] each with code, error, suggestion, path and stage.

tool.name: get_connection_hints
tool.title: How to connect a platform
tool.description: Use this FIRST when the user names a platform they want to stream to ("put this on YouTube", "also send it to Twitch") and there is no destination for it yet. Returns, for that platform: the connection methods, the exact `ingestUrl` to pass to create_rtmp_destination (or null when the platform issues one per session), what each method can and cannot do afterwards, the Streamloop tools to call in order, where in the platform's own UI the user finds the stream key, and the behaviour that otherwise ends a 24/7 loop early. NEVER guess an ingest url — a wrong host is a stream that silently never connects. Static guidance: it reads nothing, changes nothing and costs nothing. YouTube in particular has TWO answers and they are not equivalent: a managed connection (Google consent, and only then can titles, privacy, thumbnails and viewer counts be managed from here) or a plain stream key (video only).

tool.description:
Step 1 of uploading a LOCAL file: reserves the media record and returns `uploadUrl`, a presigned PUT you can use immediately. This server does not relay bytes, but YOU probably can — if the client can run a command or make an HTTP request, do the PUT itself:
  curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: <the mimeType you passed>' --data-binary @<file> '<uploadUrl>'
The Content-Type header MUST equal the mimeType given here, or the signature is rejected. The url is valid for about 11 hours and takes the whole file in one request (up to 5 GB; a bigger file, up to 15 GB, must come in through import_upload_from_url). If the client cannot make requests, hand `uploadUrl` to the user. Then call complete_upload — media that is never PUT and completed stays unusable. If the file is already reachable over https (including a file the user attached in this conversation), skip all of this and use discover_external_media + import_upload_from_url instead. Returns object (the media record: id obj_..., name, type, mimeType, fileSize, uploaded false, createdAt), uploadUrl and next (the next step).

Viewers see it at once. The arguments are checked first, then against what is published (a frame, control, table or playlist source it doesn't have, a toggle given "yes": INVALID_INPUT); only then is it refused while nothing plays it (SCENE_OFFLINE). A SCENE_TIMEOUT may or may not have applied: send an actionId (a new uuid per action, kept by you) and retry with the SAME actionId and arguments — it is applied at most once. Without an actionId, never retry an action that isn't idempotent (skip, a button) blind: read get_scene_state first. Needs a stream playing the published scene (set_stream_scene, start_stream); it changes what is on air, never the draft. Answers streamId, online, frame (on air after the action) and next.
